components.source_check: Feller V.2 p.137 median definition, V.5 p.148 notation -F, symmetric law, symmetrization: present except the density form of symmetry.
components.gap: Feller's definition of symmetry (V.5, p.148: "The distribution F is called symmetric if -F = F. [When a density f exists this means that f(-x) = f(x).]") includes a density form that the handbook does not supply: feller-weak-law-presentation.tex 36-41 defines symmetry only as equality of the laws of X and -X. Supply the density form (for a law with density f, symmetry holds exactly when f(-x) = f(x) for almost every x, equivalently when f has an even version) with its proof, in the editable Feller host.

components.source_check: Feller (5.1)-(5.3) (p.148) in exact left-limit form with the continuity-point source forms; existence of a median, centering by a median; the general interval statement of non-uniqueness (p.137) is narrowed to one example.
components.gap: Feller's median paragraph (V.2, p.137) states that if F(x) = 1/2 for all x of an interval [a,b] then every such x is a median. The handbook (body 46, annex 21-22) gives only the fair-sign instance of non-uniqueness; supply the general interval statement with its proof in the editable Feller host.

Feller p.150: M is the first term greatest in absolute value, T = S_n - M.

Feller Lemma 2, (5.9)-(5.13) (pp.149-150): symmetry of S, the four-sign joint law, (5.9) with the zero-remainder mass, the non-strict comparison written out step by step (annex 147-179), the exact maximum probabilities, and (5.10) at every t > 0 including atoms.
Feller (6.1)-(6.2) (p.150) with the (a,b] convention and the 2Mh partition estimate written in full.
Feller (7.6)-(7.7), (7.9) (p.235): tau, sigma and the truncated means, with closed and half-open endpoint conventions.
Feller (7.7) identity by integration by parts and footnote 11 (both directions of tau -> 0 iff sigma -> 0, the converse proved by a dyadic estimate).
Feller (7.2)-(7.5) (pp.234-235): the i.i.d. lemma is supplied with a correct n^{-1} variance coefficient; the remark that (7.4) holds for dependent variables with varying distributions is not.
components.gap: Feller remarks (VII.7, p.235) that inequality (7.4), P{|S_n - m'_n| > t} <= P{|S'_n - m'_n| > t} + P{S_n != S'_n}, "is valid also for dependent variables with varying distributions". The handbook states the truncation estimate only for independent X_k with a common law (body 201-217) and uses the event inclusion only inside that proof (annex 345-352), so this hypothesis-weakening variant is omitted. State and prove (7.4) for arbitrary, possibly dependent and non-identically distributed X_k truncated at a fixed level, before specializing to the i.i.d. Chebyshev bound.

components.source_check: Feller VII.7 Theorem 1 (7.8)-(7.9) and proof (pp.235-236): sufficiency via the lemma with s = n, necessity via V.(5.6), the largest-term exponential bound (strict form, as the chain needs) and V.(5.7), and the passage to tau(t) -> 0 written out.
Feller p.236 discussion: finite-mean case, symmetric laws without expectation, and (on the route elsewhere) the strong law requiring an expectation; the historical claims of pp.234-235 are omitted.
components.gap: Feller's VII.7 records two historical claims about the classical law (7.1) that the finite-mean corollary (body 248-257, annex 462-470) omits: p.234 calls the finite-variance statement (7.1) the oldest version of the law of large numbers, and p.235 names the finite-expectation statement "Khintchine's law of large numbers". Record both, with the source locators, in the editable Feller host.
